nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

## Model Links
[🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

**vae**

- [minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors)
- [minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors)

**diffusion_models**

- [minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/diffusion_models/minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors)

**text_encoders**

- [qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors)

**loras**

- 4 steps: [minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1_comfyui_bf16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/loras/minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1_comfyui_bf16.safetensors)

**embeddings**

- [10 style embeddings](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/tree/main/embeddings) (`minimaxh3_*.safetensors`), for example `minimaxh3_art_is_explosion`

## Model Storage Location

```
📂 ComfyUI/
├── 📂 models/
│   ├── 📂 vae/
│   │   ├── minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors
│   │   └── minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors
│   ├── 📂 diffusion_models/
│   │   └── minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors
│   ├── 📂 text_encoders/
│   │   └── qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors
│   ├── 📂 loras/
│   │   └── minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1_comfyui_bf16.safetensors
│   └── 📂 embeddings/
│       └── minimaxh3_art_is_explosion.safetensors
```

## Using Prompt Embeddings

Prompt embeddings (supported since [ComfyUI#15697](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15697)) add reusable style tokens to your prompt. Download one or more embeddings from the folder above into `ComfyUI/models/embeddings/`, then reference one in the prompt text with the `embedding:` prefix and the filename without its extension, for example:

`embedding:minimaxh3_art_is_explosion`

Using an embedding is optional and the template runs fine without one.

## Report Issue

Note: Please update ComfyUI first ([guide](https://docs.comfy.org/installation/update_comfyui)) and prepare required models. Desktop/Cloud updates follow stable releases, so some nightly-supported models may not be available yet.

- Cannot run / runtime errors: [ComfyUI/issues](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI/issues)
- UI / frontend issues: [ComfyUI_frontend/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_frontend/issues)
- Workflow issues: [workflow_templates/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/issues)

subject_definitions:
<Video 1> is the five-frame audiovisual continuation source. It establishes the fixed orbital camera, the completed impact behind the upper-right planetary limb, the opening white sensor saturation, and the synchronized electronic overload.

<Picture 2> is a state-reference image for the damaged planetary condition. It preserves the same alien planet identity, same geography, same orientation, a darkened impact-facing hemisphere, broad red-orange geological fissures, a dense upper-right ejecta field, and subtle local disruption of the equatorial orbital infrastructure. It is a state reference, not a separate new planet.

<Subject 1> is the solid alien planet from <Picture 1> and <Picture 2>, preserving its coherent spherical shape, exact orientation, blue-purple geography, cratered cellular terrain, recognizable basin and land layout, and overall planetary scale.

<Subject 2> is the planet's atmosphere and weather system from <Picture 1>, including the thin blue atmospheric limb, cloud cover, northern cyclone, southern cyclone, and cyan upper-atmospheric aurora.

<Subject 3> is the cyan-teal surface-light network from <Picture 1>, fixed precisely to the terrain. Its branch geometry remains static while its illumination fails.

<Subject 4> is the thin equatorial orbital-infrastructure band from <Picture 1> and <Picture 2>, composed of extremely small discontinuous structures and lights. It is not a solid ring.

<Subject 5> is the already-existing far-side impact wound and ejecta field, originating behind the fixed upper-right horizon. It consists of a compact white-blue vapor source, a dense dark particulate ejecta curtain, sparse angular crustal fragments, and minimal molten ejecta.

<Subject 6> is one thin atmospheric-ablation boundary expanding across the spherical surface from the fixed hidden upper-right impact origin.

<Subject 7> is the damaged planetary wake revealed behind <Subject 6>, based on the state shown in <Picture 2>: exposed charcoal-black terrain, broad irregular red-orange geological fissures, missing cloud cover, extinguished artificial illumination, weakened cyclones, disrupted aurora, and a thinner asymmetrical atmosphere.

summary:
[video continuation + reference generation + audio reference] The target continues directly from <Video 1>. Exposure recovers onto the same already-hit alien planet. The far-side ejecta field is immediately visible behind the upper-right limb. One thin diagonal atmospheric-ablation boundary begins crossing the visible hemisphere, slanting from upper-right toward lower-left in projection, and progressively reveals the same planet in a scorched damaged state informed by <Picture 2>. The clip ends during the transition, before the final damaged state is fully complete.

retention_analysis:
<Video 1> (opening continuation): fully_preserved - the camera, planet orientation, impact location, whiteout, and synchronized overload continue without a scene change.
<Picture 2> (damaged-state guidance): partially_preserved - its damaged hemisphere, ejecta direction, fissure behavior, and local orbital disruption guide the revealed aftermath without replacing the original planet identity.
<Subject 1> (entire video): fully_preserved - the same geography, spherical body, orientation, and apparent diameter remain recognizable.
<Subject 2> (entire video): partially_preserved - cloud cover, cyclones, aurora, and atmospheric symmetry begin degrading behind the boundary.
<Subject 3> (entire video): partially_preserved - the terrain-locked network remains fixed while its illumination progressively extinguishes.
<Subject 4> (entire video): partially_preserved - the band remains mostly organized while one short impact-facing sector flickers and dims.
<Subject 5> (entire video): fully_preserved - the wound and ejecta remain rooted behind the same upper-right horizon.
<Subject 6> (mid-video): fully_preserved - one narrow slanted boundary remains attached to the atmosphere and centered on the hidden impact origin.
<Subject 7> (mid-to-late video): fully_preserved - the wake remains visibly scorched, fissured, cloud-reduced, electrically damaged, and atmospherically depleted.

detailed_description:
Photorealistic high-end orbital catastrophe shot. One continuous inertially locked wide shot. Constant focal length, constant framing, and constant apparent planet diameter. No camera push, pullback, reframing, or rotation. The impact has already happened. No second projectile, no second impact, no new detonation, no detached shock ring, and no jagged deformation of the planetary silhouette.

[Shot 1] Begin inside the white sensor saturation from <Video 1>. Exposure decreases rapidly. Black space returns first around the frame edges. The left hemisphere of <Subject 1> resolves next. The upper-right planetary limb remains saturated longest. The same planet returns in exactly the same location, orientation, and scale.

At 00:00.700, <Subject 5> is already visible behind the upper-right horizon. A compact white-blue vapor source illuminates a directional ejecta field extending into black space on the right. Dark particulate material dominates. The ejecta appears as a dense granular silicate curtain mixed with sparse angular crustal fragments. Large fragments are mostly black in silhouette with only short incandescent edges. Fine particulate material expands ballistically and partially occludes background stars. The ejecta does not billow like smoke. Molten ejecta is sparse and produces no long luminous trails and no random fireballs.

At 00:01.200, <Subject 3> begins failing across the impact-facing hemisphere. Connected branches flicker and extinguish in place through their existing geometry. Failed regions remain dark.

At 00:01.700, <Subject 6> appears just below the upper-right impact region as one short, thin, irregular crescent. In screen projection, the boundary is clearly diagonal, leaning from upper-right toward lower-left at roughly a 35 to 45 degree angle relative to the equatorial orbital band. It is not vertical. As it advances, it lengthens diagonally while translating leftward across the visible hemisphere. Every point on the boundary remains centered on the fixed hidden upper-right impact origin.

The boundary remains no thicker than two percent of the planet’s apparent diameter. It is a narrow atmospheric-ablation interface, not a glowing graphic line, not a solid wall, not a transparent dome, and not a detached ring.

The boundary does not cover the surface. It strips cloud cover and reveals <Subject 7> directly behind it. The same alien geography remains visible, but the terrain becomes darker, scorched, and regionally fractured. Broad red-orange geological fissures begin appearing in large connected structures. The wake shows large dark burned regions and thick molten fractures, never tiny gold city-light patterns and never Earth-like coastlines.

At 00:03.000, the diagonal boundary reaches the northern cyclone. Its outer bands shear, its eye elongates, and cloud coherence weakens severely.

At 00:03.700, the cyan aurora briefly overbrightens, bends away from the impact origin, and breaks into unstable filaments. The blue atmospheric limb behind the boundary becomes thinner and more irregular.

At 00:04.800, the boundary approaches the southern cyclone. The storm begins losing spiral definition. The damaged wake behind the front remains exposed and readable rather than hidden beneath a cloud cap.

At 00:05.200, a short impact-facing sector of <Subject 4> flickers and dims. A small dark discontinuity appears, but the rest of the orbital band remains intact. No chain of explosions occurs.

From 00:05.800 onward, motion becomes slower and more readable. The ejecta field continues expanding outward. The slanted boundary continues its diagonal upper-right to lower-left progression while translating leftward across the planet. The damaged wake remains clearly visible as the same alien terrain in a progressively scorched, fissured, and depleted state. End while the planet is still in transition, before the full final devastated state is complete.

overall_soundscape:
The opening sensor overload falls into brief near-silence as exposure recovers. A narrow electronic recovery tone and unstable telemetry return gradually. Surface-network failure produces short clipped signal dropouts. Atmospheric stripping is accompanied by a restrained low-frequency sensor vibration. No conventional explosion boom and no music.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A
